title: Boys Run The Riot
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: High-schooler Ryo knows he is transgender but has no one to confide in: not his best friend, on whom he has a crush, and not his mother, who keeps asking why Ryo dresses like a boy. He discovers that Jin, a transfer student who looks like a bully, shares his taste in streetwear, and the two start a clothing brand together. The four-volume seinen drama by a transgender author follows Ryo's coming out and self-expression through fashion.
life_message: Living as your true self, with friends who accept you, is worth the fear of being seen.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Ryo seeks acceptance and dignity, not revenge on bullies.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Breaking school and family expectations to dress freely (Kodansha blurb).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Chosen friends over family expectations (AniList Found Family).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Peers build a brand together as equals.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Clothes as the vehicle of self-expression.

folkways.japan: School pressure to conform (dress codes, gendered uniforms) and reluctance to discuss gender openly reflect Japanese social expectations around harmony and appearance.

delivery.evidence: ANN manga guide: "a story about living authentically"; growth shown through choices; neither reviewer calls it preachy.
delivery.note: Authenticity is carried by plot; ANN reviewers describe opposition mainly as general pressure, with some bullies drawn simply.

winners_losers: Ryo and his friends build a brand and a place to belong; conformist pressure and transphobic classmates lose sympathy.
